evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Describes the user need (creating a game) without prescribing specific UI widgets or implementation mechanisms beyond basic input.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Specifies the need to invite via a link; does not mandate technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Unnecessarily prescribes a concrete UI widget (a single multi-line text field) rather than just the need to enter an item to estimate.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (visibility of items) without prescribing a specific solution.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the capability needed (choose an item) without dictating UI/technical design.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Focuses on the need to add items; no concrete implementation prescribed.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: States the need to edit items without specifying how it must be implemented.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Describes required functionality (remove an item) without solution details.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Captures a moderation need (reveal estimates early) without prescribing UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific algorithm/decision rule (average) rather than the underlying need (record/derive an agreed estimate).

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete UI element behavior (a particular field auto-filled) and a specific trigger condition, prescribing solution details.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: States the need to record the agreed estimate without prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to re-estimate; does not dictate how re-estimation is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific source/format (spreadsheet) as the mechanism rather than the general need to bulk import stories.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Mandates a specific interaction mechanism (copy/paste) and source (spreadsheet), which are solution choices.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Expresses the need to find prior games without prescribing UI or technical implementation.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: States an information access need without specifying storage format or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a concrete output/storage format (HTML file), which is a solution choice rather than the underlying need to export/save.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific export format (CSV), a solution detail rather than the stakeholder need to export data for processing.

evaluations.evidence: so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Includes a concrete data-handling mechanism (no longer stored) that prescribes storage behavior rather than just the need to remove a game.

evaluations.evidence: by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Over-specifies the solution/UI data fields required for account creation instead of the need to create an account.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific authentication mechanism/credentials (account name + password) rather than the need to authenticate.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: States the need to update account information without prescribing how or which fields/controls.

evaluations.evidence: so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Specifies a storage-level implementation outcome (no longer stored) rather than the user need to delete an account.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a user need (localized time display) without prescribing technical approach.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific recovery mechanism/channel (email password reminder) rather than the broader need to regain access.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Over-prescribes specific estimation scales/values (solution choice) instead of the need to choose an estimation scale.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Imposes a concrete numeric limit (15) which is a design/constraint choice rather than a pure stakeholder need.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes specific UI/interaction details (enter name on a page accessed via URL) rather than the need to join a game.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: States an information need without prescribing presentation or implementation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Expresses visibility need; no solution details mandated.

evaluations.evidence: see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need for status/attribution visibility without prescribing UI widgets or mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Defines desired behavior/outcome (simultaneous reveal after all submitted) without specifying implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card
evaluations.rationale: States a rule/need about when changes are allowed; does not prescribe technical mechanisms or UI widgets.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Expresses an information need without prescribing storage format or UI design.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: States the need for transparency during discussion without solution prescription.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific mechanism and parameter (a countdown timer of two minutes) rather than the general need to timebox discussion.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Specifies concrete solution behavior tied to a particular timer feature and trigger condition, prescribing implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Describes the need to review prior information; 'scroll back' is not a concrete widget/implementation mandate in this context.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: States a consistency need (stable ordering) without prescribing how ordering is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a rule about allowed changes; does not prescribe UI/technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes concrete UI design elements (small thumbnail photo, placement near cards) rather than the underlying need for personalization/identity cues.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Mandates specific technical standards/implementation choices (XHTML/CSS compliance) rather than the stakeholder need (broad accessibility/compatibility).

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: States a documentation/communication need without prescribing technical implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Directly prescribes a technical mechanism (database indexes) instead of the need (fast queries/performance).

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Over-specifies concrete platform targets/versions (solution constraint) rather than the general need for broad browser compatibility.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a specific standard (W3C guidelines) as the solution approach rather than the need (accessibility).

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: States a performance need without prescribing technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a capability need (support many languages/characters); does not prescribe specific implementation beyond the general standard name.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Prescribes a solution-level artifact (URL structure) rather than the underlying need (transparent navigation/shareability).

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: States a user experience need for understandable failures without mandating specific UI widgets or technical mechanisms.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Expresses a stakeholder need (non-identifiable storage/privacy) without prescribing specific storage formats or anonymization algorithms.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: States an information need (usage metrics) without prescribing how metrics are collected or displayed.
